summary: No blocking security issues. The workflow trusts nothing from the event. The script reads the PR and its comments live, and counts a plan comment only from an author with admin, maintain or write permission (collaborators API, not author_association). Logins are checked against a strict regex before they reach a URL. Line 1 is capped at 256 characters, must match an exact marker regex, and must carry a phase and status from fixed lists. Only fixed strings reach the `label=` and `reason=` outputs, so a crafted comment can't inject a key (the smuggle case is tested). `pull_request_target` runs no PR code. The only checkout is this repo, with an SHA-pinned action and `persist-credentials: false`. Permissions are `{}` at the top and least-privilege on the job. Event values reach the scripts through `env:` only, never `${{ }}` in `run:`. `GITHUB_TOKEN` label writes start no workflows, so there is no cascade. The caller template's `if:` precedence is correct. Residual risk: any writer can set the label, which is by design. The script also removes any `pr:*` label, including ones not made by this tool, which is harmless.
